program.section_heading: Conflict Resolution and Mediation - Certificate of Achievement: City
outcomes: Contemplate, analyze, and discuss issues related to the role of culture in conflict resolution and mediation.
Think about their role in society through the use of conflict resolution and mediation.
Critically think about their own values, individual biases, and personal conflict resolution style.
Discover the art and science of conflict resolution and mediation.
Learn and understand the core principles, values, and application of conflict resolution and mediation.
Develop and enhance skills related to communication, listening and problem solving.

notes: Outcomes are printed for 'the Conflict Resolution and Mediation Program' as a whole; this certificate is the only award in the section, so they are recorded here. The lead-in 'Students who complete the Conflict Resolution and Mediation Program will be able to:' runs into the first outcome on the same line and was removed.
PSYC 130 is printed first with 'OR PSYC 166'; PSYC 166 (closed list) is recorded as the alternative.

The summary mentions students entering 'the academic and/or professional fields related to Conflict Resolution and Mediation'; this was not recorded as a named career. Career-related wording in course descriptions (e.g., counseling, human services) was not used.
The requirements table prints a stray '3.0' before each 'or' pair, apparently the units for the pair as a whole; the block total of 18.0 matches six 3-unit choices.
